text:
support_jt: Customer (Acme Corp) opened a ticket — private VPC apps failing to call our hosted API when company HTTP proxy is enabled. Errors are intermittent: either connection reset or TLS verify failures. Happening from multiple hosts in the VPC. Need quick triage and suggested remediation so they can unblock.

alex: thanks. can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and any client-side TLS error? Also which proxy (squid/f5/bluecoat)?

support_jt: they say "BlueCoat SESS-Proxy" but no exact version. Repro they gave:

```
curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:3128 https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
*   Trying proxy.corp:3128...
* Connected to proxy.corp (10.10.1.5) port 3128 (#0)
> CONNECT api.redwood-inference.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood-inference.com\r\nProxy-Connection: Keep-Alive\r\n\r\n
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established\r\n\r\n
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* SSLv3, TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* SSL: certificate subject: CN=Corp TLS Intercept
* SSL: certificate verify result: self signed certificate in certificate chain (18), continuing
curl: (60) SSL: certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain

```

support_jt: sometimes instead of cert error they see a TCP reset during handshake (connection reset by peer). So two failure modes: MITM cert mismatch OR abrupt reset.

raj: this looks like classic TLS interception + some policies that occasionally drop CONNECT after establishing the connection. The key clues: "HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established" then a proxy cert is presented (MITM) — that explains the verify failure if customer doesn't trust the proxy CA. The reset could be caused by deep inspection workflows that terminate tunnels when they hit certain ALPN/cipher combos or when SNI is missing/rewritten.

maria: if the proxy is performing TLS interception, they need to either: 1) add the proxy CA to their service truststore (not great for security), or 2) configure the proxy to allow passthrough for api.redwood-inference.com (no intercept), or 3) add a proxy rule to allow CONNECT+TLS passthrough for that hostname/IP. Recommend option 2 or 3.

alex: two extra troubleshooting commands to confirm behavior from inside their VPC:

```
# 1) show proxy CONNECT status (curl shows the 200 and cert)
curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:3128 https://api.redwood-inference.com/

# 2) check server cert presented after CONNECT via openssl (without trusting proxy CA)
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com
# run this from a host that is NOT configured to use the proxy (to see real cert)
```

alex: if openssl run from a non-proxied host shows our real cert (CN=*.redwood-inference.com, valid chain) but curl via proxy shows the proxy CA, that's confirmation of interception.

support_jt: customer ran openssl from another host (no proxy) and got the expected cert. Running curl via proxy shows proxy CN.

raj: another important angle — many enterprise proxies rewrite or strip the TLS SNI when performing CONNECT (especially if they terminate early or do TLS offloading). We rely on SNI in our edge routing for some multi-tenant SNI-based host selection. If SNI is removed or replaced with a generic value, the request can be routed to a default backend which may not accept the ALPN/ciphers expected and the connection can be reset. Ask the proxy team to preserve SNI during CONNECT passthrough or add an exception for our hostname.

maria: also ask them to check header rewriting. Some proxies rewrite Host headers or add internal headers which can confuse our upstream routing and auth checks. If the proxy rewrites Host -> "internal-host" we may reject the request or trigger a different TLS profile.

support_jt: we requested proxy logs. They returned this snippet (from proxy debug):

```
[proxy-debug] CONNECT api.redwood-inference.com:443 from 10.10.2.3
[proxy-debug] action=intercept tls=enabled icap=off
[proxy-debug] presented-ca=Corp-TLS-Intercept-CA
[proxy-debug] sni= (empty)
[proxy-debug] decision=terminate-when-policy-match
[proxy-debug] policy=inspection-high-risk -> reset-on-handshake
```

alex: that explains both modes: sni empty -> our edge sometimes picks wrong cert -> cert mismatch/errors. policy=inspection-high-risk + reset-on-handshake explains intermittent resets when the inspection engine flags the connection.

raj: mitigation options for customer (ordered by recommended):
- Add an allowlist rule on the proxy to passthrough CONNECT to api.redwood-inference.com:443 (no TLS interception).
- If passthrough is impossible, configure the proxy to preserve/forward SNI and stop terminating the TLS session for that hostname.
- As a temporary workaround, install the proxy CA into the container/VM truststore so TLS verify passes (only if permitted by security team).
- Allow direct egress to our IPs for that service via firewall rule (if policy allows IP-based exceptions, note IPs may change so prefer hostname passthrough).

maria: for the truststore approach include steps (example for debian-hosted app):

```
# add corp proxy CA to system trust
sudo cp corp-proxy.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp-proxy.pem
sudo update-ca-certificates
# restart application service
sudo systemctl restart my-app
```

support_jt: customer prefers not to add CA. They've asked us for a short justification they can give their proxy team to open passthrough. Can we provide a one-paragraph ask?

alex: draft for proxy team:

"Request: Allow CONNECT passthrough (no TLS interception) for api.redwood-inference.com:443 from the Acme VPC egress range. Reason: Redwood's hosted inference platform uses SNI-based routing and specific TLS profiles; interception currently strips SNI and/or presents the proxy CA which breaks TLS verification and causes routing mismatches or handshake resets. Passthrough will preserve end-to-end TLS and avoid certificate mistrust or intermittent connection resets. If passthrough cannot be applied hostname-based, please allow for the specific IP CIDR range we communicate and ensure the proxy preserves SNI."

support_jt: pinging customer ops for logs and confirmation. created ticket in zendesk: ZEND-48291 (eng-oncall-bot).

eng-oncall-bot: Ticket ZEND-48291 assigned to eng-support, priority P2.

customer_ops_bot: customer confirmed proxy team applied a passthrough rule for api.redwood-inference.com for their egress range. After change, they report calls succeed consistently. They did not install CA.

support_jt: confirmed with customer: after passthrough, curl via proxy shows direct server cert and no verify errors. They ran smoke tests for model calls, latency looks normal. Closing loop with them and recommended long-term: maintain passthrough for our hostnames or configure proxy to forward SNI.

maria: add note for security: if they absolutely must inspect traffic, consider mTLS with us (contact sales/enterprise) so interception is unnecessary. Otherwise document truststore steps and the security tradeoffs.

alex: marking resolved from eng side. :white_check_mark:

support_jt: closing thread, will update zendesk and the customer. :thumbsup:
